newsitem.title: USA: U.S W.Coast crude weighed by NYMEX, traders absent.
newsitem.headline: U.S W.Coast crude weighed by NYMEX, traders absent.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices eased in inactive Monday trade, pressured by lower domestic markets, traders said.
Local West Coast trade failed to get going with most players attending an industry rafting trip sponsored by Tosco Corp on Monday and Tuesday, traders said.
The largest producer of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, the regional benchmark, offered the grade at $1.60 off July West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
Meanwhile, crude oil futures for July delivery eased 11 cents a barrel Monday, amid ample supplies.
Buyers expect the next ANS cargo to sell wider than $2.25 a barrel off July WTI.
Traders said a malfunctioning crude disillation unit at ARCO's Carson, Calif, refinery this weekend could cause crude inventories to rise at the plant if damage is significant.
"It would make crude sloppier, and margins a little tighter," one trader said, referring to the effect on crude oil and refined petroleum products prices, respectively.
If the unit shuts, traders said, ARCO would have to buy refined products from other refiners, cutting into supply.
